analysis:
Units examined: ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head lines 1044-1689 and ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (patch plus base text). The visible ModelLoading lines are entirely outside the changed head ranges (the last changed range ends at 658), so they are unchanged context: load gate arithmetic, unloadModel, evictUntilAvailable, fastAdmissionReject, loadErrorStatusCode. I found no regression in that context. The changed ModelLoading hunks (the injectable `loadWeightHasher` closure replacing the direct WeightHasher.computeHash call, and the managed-GLM verified-digest path around lines 542-563 and 615-624) are only partly visible in the truncated patch excerpt and were not reviewed in full.

Serve.swift's only change is line 108: `if usesHostServices { verifiedWeightHashesFile = VerifiedWeightHashStore.path() }`, which arms a persistent verified-weight-hash file for the real serving loop and not for test instances. The code at that point sets only a path. The VerifiedWeightHashStore implementation, its file permissions, its integrity and tamper resistance, and how persisted hashes are consumed were not supplied. I cannot tell whether a locally writable hash file lets an operator (ADV-001, T-012, T-027) substitute weights and have a stale or forged hash reported as verified in `liveModelHashes` and `loadedModelHashesSnapshot`. I cannot tell whether the hash feeds the SSD cache weightHash binding (T-041) either. The surrounding code shows `SSDPrefixCacheFactory.verifiedWeightHash` is used to gate the hash value. Open questions for the next pass: (1) does the persisted store get re-validated against the snapshotFingerprint before reuse; (2) is the file owner-only, written atomically, and kept out of the attestation or coordinator-reported trust path; (3) does the `loadWeightHasher` injection default to the real WeightHasher in production, with no test hook reachable in release builds. No concrete finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
